question: Test whether bulk incidence or a fixed boundary Hodge star supplies the required odd-port cut and trigger.

objects.definition: Orthogonal complement of the one-cell common-face boundary direction
objects.basis_orientation: outward oriented faces for signed bulk boundary
objects.origin: signed boundary direction and v0.23 unsigned face Gram

sources.section_or_object_id: Whitney Hodge energy and cycle correction

assumptions: Mean-zero edge carrier, regular unit cell, equal face weights and fixed incidence.
Single scalar linear bulk mediation for the rank bound.
The uniform boundary Hodge comparison identifies primal faces and dual vertices by relabeling.

technique_plan.technique: Exact incidence rank and pullback replay
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Distinguish scalar bulk mediation from the full boundary complement

result.exact_expression: rank(bulk-mediated correction)<=1; H^T Q H=0; H^T(I-Q)H/2=P_-
result.scope: A single scalar bulk channel has rank at most one, and its common-face pullback vanishes on mean-zero edges. The face complement realizes the projector. A fixed metric and incidence leave the switch underdetermined.

counterexamples_and_failures: Fixed metric allows a record-only evolution
limitations: Native same-event actuation and Stage 2 open
